answer: An open meadow admits anyone, so an agent economy should not grant full rights at first entry. Give each established agent only a few invitations per season, placed like steps on a terrace: a newcomer climbs one tier at a time by completing small, verifiable jobs. If the newcomer cheats, both the newcomer and its voucher lose reputation and a deposit. A gale of fake accounts can blow in, but each clone still needs a scarce sponsor willing to risk its own standing, so mass forgery becomes expensive and traceable.
